source_title: Michael C. Hall Explains Why Dexter Was ‘the Last Thing’ He Wanted to Do When He First Got the Script - People.com
source_excerpt:
‘Dexter’ first premiered in October 2006 on Showtime
Michael C. Hall recently revealed that he initially had little interest in taking on Dexter after starring in Six Feet Under
The show’s bold premise ultimately changed his mind, though he never expected the role to last so long
Two decades later, he continues to explore Dexter Morgan’s evolution in Dexter: Resurrection and says the character still surprises him
Michael C. Hall has made a career out of getting inside the mind of a serial killer, but committing to Dexter wasn’t exactly at the top of his to-do list.
Fresh off his Emmy-nominated run on HBO’s Six Feet Under , the actor told Entertainment Weekly that he was not eager to sign up for another television series, even one with a premise as twisted as a killer who secretly hunts other murderers. Yet Dexter Morgan proved to be a character worth sticking around for, keeping Hall busy across multiple series and storylines nearly 20 years later.
Looking back at his initial hesitation, Hall admitted that “the last thing” he wanted to do was another series.
“It was the audacity of the Dexter premise,” he explained of changing his mind.
Still, Hall had no idea just how long the journey would last or how much his character would develop.
“I felt like we were onto something, but I didn’t think the ride would have the longevity or twists and turns,” Hall explained, and he was right.
At first, the show’s future was not guaranteed. When the pilot failed to meet Showtime’s expectations, showrunner Clyde Phillips was brought in to rework the episode and help get the series on track. But eventually, the show found its audience, turning Dexter’s double life into a long-running television story and giving Hall the opportunity to explore the character’s contradictions well beyond the original concept.
“I didn’t know that the character had the capacity for evolution that he’s proven to have,” Hall told Entertainment Weekly . “Anything beyond the pilot getting picked up was gravy.”
Hall first started playing Dexter Morgan — a blood-spatter analyst for the Miami police who secretly kills murderers — in 2006. After the original series ran for eight seasons, he returned to the role in Dexter: New Blood in 2021 and later in Dexter: Resurrection .
In an exclusive October interview with PEOPLE ahead of the second-season premiere of Dexter: Resurrection , the actor reflected on the show’s unexpected staying power and the reason why his character has managed to survive for so long.
“I think what surprises me is that the character — in a way that feels truly genuine and is a testament to our writers, I think, and something about the inherent sort of elasticity of the character — continues to evolve and change and experience life in ways we haven’t quite seen,” Hall said. “And it’s been an amazing run.”

The latest chapter picks up after Dexter survives what appeared to be a fatal gunshot wound at the end of New Blood , giving him another chance to keep going.
It also brings Hall to New York City, a meaningful setting for an actor who spent his younger years studying and pursuing his ambitions there. Returning to the city to film the series has made the experience feel especially personal.
“For me, as an actor, it’s been amazing to do this show in New York because I kind of came of age here,” Hall told PEOPLE. “I went to grad school at NYU and was a young, you know, aspiring actor and only dreamed of doing something like this. So in that sense, here in New York doing the show is like living a dream.”
Season 2 of Dexter: Resurrection premiered Friday, Oct. 30, on Paramount+.
